questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how Update keeps the cache and the repository consistent? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
After SetChannel succeeds for a user, what happens on the next Get for that user?
choices: It returns the entry cached before SetChannel, until the TTL expires
It fails with ErrNotFound because the key was removed
It misses the cache, loads from the repository, and repopulates the cache
It reads the new value directly from SetChannel's in-memory copy

questions.prompt: Why does SetChannel call s.repo.Load instead of s.Get before modifying the preferences?
choices: Get is not safe to call concurrently
A cached copy may be stale or may not have been persisted, so a read-modify-write on it could overwrite newer saved changes
Get does not return a pointer that can be modified
Load is faster than Get because it bypasses JSON decoding

questions.prompt: The cache backend is down: Get and Set on it fail (Get reports a miss, Set returns errors). What is the effect on Get for a user whose preferences exist in the repository?
choices: Get returns an error because fill reports the cache failure
Get returns the preferences from the repository on every call, with each call going to the repository
Get retries the cache until it recovers
